title: Terahertz fingerprints and machine learning for complementary discrimination of medicinal materials
article_type: Submitted Papers / original research; match the portal option
abstract: Routine identification of medicinal materials relies on established morphological, microscopic and chemical tests. Developing terahertz spectroscopy as a complementary tool requires useful discrimination and an understanding of how spectral processing and labelled specimens contribute to prediction. We present a budget-controlled workflow that aggregates multiclass coefficient-stability scores, selects retained variables and SVM settings within nested validation, and traces the information used for prediction in 1,672 specimens from four medicinal materials. Under leave-one-workbook-out validation, a common absorption classifier correctly classified 854/864 Suanzaoren–Zaoren specimens (98.84%) and 1097/1672 specimens across all four materials (65.61%), revealing uneven cross-workbook generalization. In balanced five-source Suanzaoren analysis, selected absorption features achieved 93.44% mean accuracy with 63.95% mean variable reduction under repeated nested cross-validation. At 62 retained predictors, a joint standard-normal-variate (SNV) candidate pool achieved 87.11%, compared with 81.00% for SNV absorption and 88.78% for raw absorption. All 930 retained feature occurrences from the joint pool were absorption coordinates, identifying a change in selected absorption subsets rather than direct retention of both modalities. Support-label controls increased accuracy from 80.00% to 83.78% with standardization and kernel scale frozen, locating the main gain in valid supervision and decision-function updating. Two qualified protocatechuic-acid calculations supplied a molecular frequency reference above the modelling interval. These findings support complementary medicinal-material discrimination and provide an evidence-based framework for choosing spectral representations and label-update strategies in subsequent terahertz studies.
